options.C: Add processing units to the instance.
options.D: Move the instance to a custom instance configuration based on nam3 that adds a read-only replica in asia-northeast1, and use stale reads from Tokyo.

explanation.summary: Custom instance configurations let you add read-only replicas to a base configuration. Read-only replicas serve stale or strong reads locally without taking part in write quorums.

option_breakdown.A: A second instance needs its own pipeline and is not consistent with the first.
option_breakdown.B: asia-northeast1 is not a read-write region of nam3, and moving leaders would slow US writes.
option_breakdown.C: More compute does not remove the distance between Tokyo and the US.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. Custom instance configurations let you add read-only replicas to a base configuration. Read-only replicas serve stale or strong reads locally without taking part in write quorums.

questions.title: A one-off copy of a BigQuery dataset to another region
questions.summary: The BigQuery Data Transfer Service dataset copy copies a dataset across regions on demand or on a schedule.
questions.question: Before decommissioning a project, a team must copy a BigQuery dataset once from the US multi-region to europe-west3 for another team. It does not need ongoing replication or failover. What should it use?

options.A: Cross-region dataset replication with a replica in europe-west3.
options.B: ALTER TABLE ... SET OPTIONS(location='europe-west3') on each table.
options.C: A table snapshot in europe-west3.
options.D: A BigQuery dataset copy through the Data Transfer Service to a new dataset in europe-west3.

explanation.summary: Dataset copy moves the tables of a dataset into a dataset in another region, once or on a schedule, without setting up a replica relationship.

option_breakdown.A: Replication is ongoing and keeps the data tied to the source dataset, which is more than a one-off copy.
option_breakdown.B: A table's location cannot be changed in place.
option_breakdown.C: Snapshots stay in the source's location.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. Dataset copy moves the tables of a dataset into a dataset in another region, once or on a schedule, without setting up a replica relationship.

questions.title: Spanner backups that survive the instance's region
questions.summary: Copy Spanner backups to an instance in another region or configuration.
questions.question: A Spanner database on a regional configuration in europe-west1 is backed up daily. The team does not want a multi-region configuration, but it must be able to restore from a backup if europe-west1 is lost. What should it do?

options.A: Increase version_retention_period to seven days.
options.B: Export the database to a bucket in europe-west1.
options.C: Copy each backup to a Spanner instance in another region, and restore from the copy if needed.
options.D: Create the backups with a longer expiration.

explanation.summary: A Spanner backup lives in its instance's configuration. Copying it to an instance in another region gives a restorable backup that does not depend on europe-west1.

option_breakdown.A: Point-in-time recovery reads from the same database in the same region.
option_breakdown.B: A bucket in the same region is lost with it.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. A Spanner backup lives in its instance's configuration. Copying it to an instance in another region gives a restorable backup that does not depend on europe-west1.
option_breakdown.D: Keeping backups longer does not change where they are stored.

questions.title: A Firestore database created in the wrong location
questions.summary: A Firestore database's location is permanent; move data to a new database in the right location.
questions.question: A Firestore database was created in the regional location us-central1. The company now needs it to survive a regional outage. What must it do?

options.A: Update the existing database's location to nam5.
options.B: Enable point-in-time recovery on the existing database.
options.C: Add a read replica of the database in us-east1.
options.D: Create a new Firestore database in a multi-region location such as nam5 and move the data into it, for example with an export and import.

explanation.summary: A Firestore database's location cannot be changed after creation. Multi-region redundancy requires a database created in a multi-region location.

option_breakdown.A: Location is immutable.
option_breakdown.B: PITR restores earlier versions in the same location.
option_breakdown.C: Firestore has no user-managed read replicas; replication comes from the location type.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. A Firestore database's location cannot be changed after creation. Multi-region redundancy requires a database created in a multi-region location.

explanation.gcloud_command:
gcloud firestore databases create --database=app-mr --location=nam5
gcloud firestore export gs://exports --database=app && gcloud firestore import gs://exports/PREFIX --database=app-mr

questions.title: A global front end that fails over between Cloud Run regions
questions.summary: One global external Application Load Balancer with serverless NEGs in two regions routes around a failure.
questions.question: An API runs on Cloud Run in us-central1 and europe-west1, backed by a Spanner multi-region database. Users must reach the API through one address, and traffic must go to the other region if one region's service fails. What should you build?

options.A: A global external Application Load Balancer with a backend service containing a serverless NEG for each region.
options.B: Two regional external Application Load Balancers with round-robin DNS.
options.C: A Cloud DNS record pointing at one service's run.app URL.
options.D: A Cloud Run traffic split between the two regions.

explanation.summary: The global load balancer uses one anycast IP, routes users to the nearest healthy region, and sends traffic to the other region when one backend fails.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. The global load balancer uses one anycast IP, routes users to the nearest healthy region, and sends traffic to the other region when one backend fails.
option_breakdown.B: Round-robin DNS keeps sending clients to a failed region until records expire.
option_breakdown.C: One run.app URL is one region.
option_breakdown.D: Traffic splitting is between revisions of one service in one region, not between regions.

explanation.gcloud_command:
gcloud compute network-endpoint-groups create api-us --region=us-central1 \
  --network-endpoint-type=serverless --cloud-run-service=api
gcloud compute backend-services add-backend api-bs --global \
  --network-endpoint-group=api-us --network-endpoint-group-region=us-central1

questions.title: Keeping batch scans away from Bigtable serving traffic
questions.summary: A second cluster plus single-cluster-routing app profiles isolates batch from serving workloads.
questions.question: A Bigtable instance serves a latency-sensitive API. A nightly analytics job scans whole tables and pushes API latency up. The company also wants a copy of the data in a second region. What single change addresses both?

options.A: Add a cluster in another region and route the analytics job to it through its own single-cluster-routing app profile.
options.B: Add nodes to the existing cluster and run the job at a lower priority.
options.C: Run the analytics job against a daily table backup.
options.D: Move the analytics job to multi-cluster routing on the existing app profile.

explanation.summary: Replicated clusters hold the same data. Routing batch reads to their own cluster isolates them from serving traffic, and the second cluster is also in another region.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. Replicated clusters hold the same data. Routing batch reads to their own cluster isolates them from serving traffic, and the second cluster is also in another region.
option_breakdown.B: More nodes help, but the batch job still competes with serving on the same cluster, and there is no second region.
option_breakdown.C: Backups must be restored to a table before they can be read, and add no second region.
option_breakdown.D: Multi-cluster routing could send batch reads to the serving cluster.

explanation.gcloud_command:
gcloud bigtable clusters create tel-analytics --instance=tel --zone=us-east1-b --num-nodes=3
gcloud bigtable app-profiles create batch --instance=tel --route-to=tel-analytics

questions.title: Spanner for a team that knows PostgreSQL
questions.summary: Spanner's PostgreSQL interface offers PostgreSQL dialect and tools on Spanner's scale and availability.
questions.question: A team of PostgreSQL developers needs a relational database with unlimited horizontal scale and 99.999% availability for a new global service. They want to keep writing PostgreSQL-dialect SQL and use familiar PostgreSQL drivers. What should they choose?

options.A: Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL with high availability.
options.B: A Spanner database created with the PostgreSQL dialect.
options.C: AlloyDB for PostgreSQL with read pools.
options.D: Bigtable with a PostgreSQL client library.

explanation.summary: Spanner offers a PostgreSQL interface: a database created with the PostgreSQL dialect accepts PostgreSQL SQL and supported drivers, while running on Spanner's horizontally scaled, multi-region architecture.

option_breakdown.A: Cloud SQL scales up, not out, and HA is regional (99.99%).
option_breakdown.B: Correct. Spanner offers a PostgreSQL interface: a database created with the PostgreSQL dialect accepts PostgreSQL SQL and supported drivers, while running on Spanner's horizontally scaled, multi-region architecture.
option_breakdown.C: AlloyDB scales reads, but writes go to one primary in one region.
option_breakdown.D: Bigtable is not relational and has no PostgreSQL interface.

questions.title: Vector search next to operational PostgreSQL data
questions.summary: AlloyDB supports embeddings and vector indexes (pgvector, ScaNN) inside PostgreSQL.
questions.question: A retailer wants semantic product search using embeddings, joined with live inventory and price columns in its PostgreSQL database, without running a separate vector database. What should it use?

options.A: Memorystore for Redis holding the embeddings.
options.B: Bigtable with one column family per embedding dimension.
options.C: Cloud Storage holding the embeddings as JSON files.
options.D: AlloyDB for PostgreSQL with vector embeddings stored beside the product rows and a vector index.

explanation.summary: AlloyDB supports pgvector and its ScaNN-based index, so similarity search runs in SQL together with joins on operational data.

option_breakdown.A: That adds a second store and loses joins with inventory data.
option_breakdown.B: Bigtable has no vector similarity search over SQL joins.
option_breakdown.C: Files in a bucket cannot be queried by similarity.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. AlloyDB supports pgvector and its ScaNN-based index, so similarity search runs in SQL together with joins on operational data.

explanation.gcloud_command:
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector;
SELECT id, name FROM products ORDER BY embedding <=> $1 LIMIT 10;

questions.title: An open-source Redis-compatible managed cache
questions.summary: Memorystore for Valkey is a managed, open-source, Redis-compatible engine.
questions.question: A company wants a fully managed, in-memory cache that is compatible with the Redis protocol but based on an open-source engine governed by the Linux Foundation, to avoid licence concerns. What should it choose?

options.A: Memorystore for Memcached.
options.B: Memorystore for Valkey.
options.C: Firestore in Datastore mode.
options.D: A Redis container on Cloud Run.

explanation.summary: Valkey is an open-source fork of Redis under the Linux Foundation. Memorystore for Valkey offers it as a managed service that existing Redis clients can use.

option_breakdown.A: Memcached is not compatible with the Redis protocol or its data structures.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. Valkey is an open-source fork of Redis under the Linux Foundation. Memorystore for Valkey offers it as a managed service that existing Redis clients can use.
option_breakdown.C: Firestore is a document database, not an in-memory cache.
option_breakdown.D: Cloud Run is stateless and not a managed cache.

questions.title: Pub/Sub messages straight into BigQuery
questions.summary: A BigQuery subscription writes messages to a table with no Dataflow job or code.
questions.question: Click events are published to a Pub/Sub topic as JSON matching a BigQuery table's schema. No transformation is needed. The team wants them in BigQuery with the least infrastructure. What should it create?

options.A: A Dataflow streaming job using the Pub/Sub to BigQuery template.
options.B: A Cloud Run service that receives push messages and calls the streaming insert API.
options.C: A BigQuery subscription on the topic that writes to the table.
options.D: A scheduled BigQuery load job that reads the topic every hour.

explanation.summary: A BigQuery subscription writes each message directly into a table, using the table or topic schema, with no pipeline to run.

option_breakdown.A: Dataflow works but adds a job to run and pay for when no transformation is needed.
option_breakdown.B: A custom service is code to maintain.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. A BigQuery subscription writes each message directly into a table, using the table or topic schema, with no pipeline to run.
option_breakdown.D: Load jobs read files, not Pub/Sub topics.

questions.title: A standard pipeline without writing Beam code
questions.summary: Google-provided Dataflow templates run common pipelines from parameters only.
questions.question: An operations team must stream messages from a Pub/Sub subscription into Cloud Storage as windowed text files. Nobody on the team writes Apache Beam code. What should it use?

options.A: The Google-provided Dataflow template Pub/Sub to Text Files on Cloud Storage, launched with parameters.
options.B: A Dataproc cluster running a Spark streaming job.
options.C: A Cloud Storage lifecycle rule.
options.D: A Cloud Run function triggered on every message that appends to one object.

explanation.summary: Dataflow templates package common pipelines. You supply parameters such as input subscription and output path, and Dataflow runs the job.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. Dataflow templates package common pipelines. You supply parameters such as input subscription and output path, and Dataflow runs the job.
option_breakdown.B: Dataproc needs Spark code and a cluster to manage.
option_breakdown.C: Lifecycle rules act on existing objects; they move no messages.
option_breakdown.D: Objects are immutable, so appending per message does not work and cannot scale.

questions.title: Atomic folder renames for an analytics lake
questions.summary: Buckets with hierarchical namespace support real folders and fast, atomic folder renames.
questions.question: A Spark-based data lake on Cloud Storage commits job output by renaming a temporary folder with thousands of objects. In a flat bucket this rename is slow and not atomic. What should the team use for new data?

options.A: A bucket with Object Versioning enabled.
options.B: A bucket in the Nearline storage class.
options.C: A dual-region bucket with turbo replication.
options.D: A bucket with hierarchical namespace enabled.

explanation.summary: Hierarchical namespace gives buckets real folders; a folder rename is a single metadata operation instead of copying and deleting every object.

option_breakdown.A: Versioning keeps older generations; renames are still copy-and-delete.
option_breakdown.B: Storage class changes price, not namespace behaviour.
option_breakdown.C: Replication settings do not change how renames work.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. Hierarchical namespace gives buckets real folders; a folder rename is a single metadata operation instead of copying and deleting every object.

questions.title: Faster repeated reads of training data from a multi-region bucket
questions.summary: Anywhere Cache adds an SSD-backed zonal read cache in front of a bucket, near the compute.
questions.question: Training jobs on GPUs in us-central1-a read the same 200 TB dataset from a US multi-region bucket many times per week. Read throughput and data transfer costs are the bottleneck. What should the team add without moving the data?

options.A: Cloud CDN in front of the bucket.
options.B: Autoclass on the bucket.
options.C: An Anywhere Cache for the bucket in us-central1-a.
options.D: Object Versioning on the bucket.

explanation.summary: Anywhere Cache creates a managed SSD read cache in a zone, so repeated reads are served close to the compute with higher throughput and lower multi-region read costs.

option_breakdown.A: Cloud CDN caches content for internet clients, not for VMs inside the region.
option_breakdown.B: Autoclass changes storage classes by access pattern; it adds no cache.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. Anywhere Cache creates a managed SSD read cache in a zone, so repeated reads are served close to the compute with higher throughput and lower multi-region read costs.
option_breakdown.D: Versioning is unrelated to read performance.

explanation.gcloud_command: gcloud storage buckets anywhere-caches create gs://training-data us-central1-a --ttl=7d

questions.title: Unknown access patterns across millions of objects
questions.summary: Autoclass moves each object between classes based on its own access, with no retrieval fees.
questions.question: A bucket holds millions of user uploads. Some are read constantly, many are never read again, and nobody can predict which. The team wants cost to follow each object's actual use without writing lifecycle rules. What should it enable?

options.A: Autoclass on the bucket.
options.B: A lifecycle rule that moves everything to Coldline after 30 days.
options.C: The Archive storage class as the bucket default.
options.D: Turbo replication.

explanation.summary: Autoclass transitions each object to colder classes when it is not accessed and back to Standard when it is, without early deletion or retrieval charges.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. Autoclass transitions each object to colder classes when it is not accessed and back to Standard when it is, without early deletion or retrieval charges.
option_breakdown.B: An age-based rule moves hot objects to Coldline too, and their reads then incur retrieval fees.
option_breakdown.C: Archive makes every frequent read expensive.
option_breakdown.D: Turbo replication is about geo-redundancy, not cost by access.

questions.title: Moving an on-premises NFS share into Cloud Storage
questions.summary: Storage Transfer Service uses transfer agents to copy from on-premises file systems.
questions.question: A company must copy 80 TB from an on-premises NFS server to Cloud Storage over its 10 Gbps Interconnect, with scheduling, retries, integrity checks and incremental re-runs, without writing scripts. What should it use?

options.A: gcloud storage cp run by cron from one server.
options.B: Storage Transfer Service with transfer agents installed on-premises, in an agent pool.
options.C: BigQuery Data Transfer Service.
options.D: Transfer Appliance shipped to the data centre.

explanation.summary: Storage Transfer Service supports POSIX file system sources through agents. It is managed, scalable across agents, validates data and copies only changes on later runs.

option_breakdown.A: One cron copy lacks managed retries, parallel scale and incremental tracking.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. Storage Transfer Service supports POSIX file system sources through agents. It is managed, scalable across agents, validates data and copies only changes on later runs.
option_breakdown.C: BigQuery Data Transfer Service loads data into BigQuery, not files into Cloud Storage.
option_breakdown.D: An appliance suits cases with little network bandwidth; 10 Gbps moves 80 TB in about a day.

explanation.gcloud_command:
gcloud transfer agent-pools create onprem-pool
gcloud transfer agents install --pool=onprem-pool --count=3
gcloud transfer jobs create posix:///mnt/share gs://landing --source-agent-pool=onprem-pool

questions.title: Thousands of batch tasks on VMs without a scheduler to run
questions.summary: Google Cloud Batch provisions VMs, runs queued tasks and deletes the VMs, with no cluster to manage.
questions.question: A genomics lab runs 5,000 independent containerised tasks each night, each needing 8 vCPUs for about an hour. It does not want to run a scheduler, a cluster or clean-up scripts. What should it use?

options.A: A GKE Standard cluster with a custom job controller.
options.B: Google Cloud Batch, submitting one job with 5,000 tasks.
options.C: A managed instance group that scales on CPU utilisation.
options.D: App Engine flexible environment.

explanation.summary: Batch queues the tasks, provisions Compute Engine VMs (including Spot VMs) to run them, retries failures and removes the VMs when the job ends.

option_breakdown.A: A cluster and controller are the infrastructure the lab wants to avoid.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. Batch queues the tasks, provisions Compute Engine VMs (including Spot VMs) to run them, retries failures and removes the VMs when the job ends.
option_breakdown.C: A MIG runs identical long-lived VMs; it has no concept of a queue of tasks that finish.
option_breakdown.D: App Engine serves web applications, not batch task arrays.

explanation.gcloud_command: gcloud batch jobs submit genome-2026-09-30 --location=us-central1 --config=job.json   # taskCount: 5000

questions.title: Leaving the data centre without leaving vSphere
questions.summary: Google Cloud VMware Engine runs VMware workloads unchanged on dedicated nodes in Google Cloud.
questions.question: A company must exit its data centre in three months. It has 600 VMs on VMware vSphere, and its operations team relies on vCenter and existing VMware tooling. Refactoring or converting the VMs is out of scope. What should it choose?

options.A: Compute Engine, importing each VM image.
options.B: GKE, containerising each application.
options.C: Google Cloud VMware Engine.
options.D: Cloud Run, rebuilding each application as a container.

explanation.summary: VMware Engine provides a private VMware cloud (vSphere, vCenter, vSAN, NSX) on Google Cloud, so VMs move with VMware tools and no conversion.

option_breakdown.A: Importing to Compute Engine converts every VM, which is out of scope.
option_breakdown.B: Containerising 600 applications is a refactoring project.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. VMware Engine provides a private VMware cloud (vSphere, vCenter, vSAN, NSX) on Google Cloud, so VMs move with VMware tools and no conversion.
option_breakdown.D: Cloud Run needs each application rebuilt as a stateless container.

questions.title: Per-core licences that need physical isolation
questions.summary: Sole-tenant nodes give dedicated physical hosts for licensing and isolation requirements.
questions.question: A company brings its own Windows Server and SQL Server licences, which are counted per physical core and require the host not to be shared with other customers. What should it run the VMs on?

options.A: Spot VMs.
options.B: Shielded VMs on shared hosts.
options.C: Compute Engine sole-tenant nodes.
options.D: Cloud Run with a minimum of one instance.

explanation.summary: Sole-tenant nodes are physical servers dedicated to your project, which meets bring-your-own-licence terms tied to physical cores and hardware isolation.

option_breakdown.A: Spot VMs run on shared hosts and can be pre-empted.
option_breakdown.B: Shielded VM verifies boot integrity; it does not dedicate the host.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. Sole-tenant nodes are physical servers dedicated to your project, which meets bring-your-own-licence terms tied to physical cores and hardware isolation.
option_breakdown.D: Cloud Run runs Linux containers on shared infrastructure.

explanation.gcloud_command:
gcloud compute sole-tenancy node-templates create win-byol --node-type=n2-node-80-640 --region=us-central1
gcloud compute sole-tenancy node-groups create win-group --node-template=win-byol --target-size=2 --zone=us-central1-a

questions.title: Oracle Exadata close to Google Cloud applications
questions.summary: Oracle Database@Google Cloud runs Oracle Exadata and Autonomous Database inside Google Cloud data centres.
questions.question: An insurer's core system runs on Oracle Exadata with RAC. It is moving its application tier to GKE and wants the database in Google Cloud with low latency to GKE, on Oracle-managed Exadata infrastructure, without re-platforming to another database. What should it use?

options.A: Oracle Database@Google Cloud.
options.B: Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL after migrating the schema.
options.C: Oracle Database installed on Compute Engine VMs.
options.D: Spanner with the PostgreSQL interface.

explanation.summary: Oracle Database@Google Cloud provides Exadata and Autonomous Database services run by Oracle inside Google Cloud regions, connected to your VPC.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. Oracle Database@Google Cloud provides Exadata and Autonomous Database services run by Oracle inside Google Cloud regions, connected to your VPC.
option_breakdown.B: That is a re-platform to a different engine.
option_breakdown.C: Self-managed Oracle on VMs is not Exadata and RAC support is limited.
option_breakdown.D: Spanner is a different database and requires re-platforming.

explanation.gcloud_command: # Console > Oracle Database@Google Cloud > Exadata Database > Create infrastructure, then VM cluster

questions.title: Data encrypted while it is being processed
questions.summary: Confidential VM encrypts memory in use with hardware-based technology (AMD SEV, Intel TDX).
questions.question: A healthcare analytics workload already encrypts data at rest and in transit. A new contract requires the data to stay encrypted in memory while VMs process it. What should you use when creating the VMs?

options.A: Confidential VM on a supported machine type, such as N2D with AMD SEV.
options.B: Shielded VM with Secure Boot.
options.C: Customer-managed encryption keys on the boot disk.
options.D: Local SSD with Hyperdisk encryption.

explanation.summary: Confidential VM uses hardware memory encryption so data remains encrypted while in use, with keys that Google cannot extract.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. Confidential VM uses hardware memory encryption so data remains encrypted while in use, with keys that Google cannot extract.
option_breakdown.B: Shielded VM protects boot integrity, not memory contents.
option_breakdown.C: CMEK controls keys for data at rest.
option_breakdown.D: Disk choices concern data at rest.

questions.title: Guaranteed capacity for a known event next month
questions.summary: A future reservation requests capacity for a future time window so VMs are available when it starts.
questions.question: A retailer knows it will need 400 extra c3-standard-8 VMs in europe-west1 for a sale that starts on a known date next month. It must be sure that capacity exists then, and does not want to pay for idle VMs until then. What should it do?

options.A: Buy a three-year committed use discount today.
options.B: Create a future reservation for 400 c3-standard-8 VMs in europe-west1 for the sale's time window.
options.C: Raise the regional CPU quota to cover 400 VMs.
options.D: Create the 400 VMs now and stop them until the sale.

explanation.summary: A future reservation asks Google to hold capacity for a start time you choose, and it becomes a normal reservation when that time arrives.

option_breakdown.A: A commitment is a price discount, not a capacity guarantee for a date.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. A future reservation asks Google to hold capacity for a start time you choose, and it becomes a normal reservation when that time arrives.
option_breakdown.C: Quota is permission to use capacity, not a promise that the capacity exists.
option_breakdown.D: Stopped VMs release their host capacity, so a restart can fail if capacity is short.

questions.title: Synchronous two-zone replication for a Hyperdisk workload
questions.summary: Hyperdisk Balanced High Availability replicates a disk synchronously across two zones.
questions.question: A database VM on a new machine series that supports only Hyperdisk needs its data disk replicated synchronously to a second zone, so a standby VM there can take over with no data loss. What disk type should you use?

options.A: Hyperdisk Extreme with daily snapshots.
options.B: Hyperdisk Balanced High Availability, replicated across two zones.
options.C: Regional Persistent Disk (pd-balanced), which every machine series supports.
options.D: Local SSD mirrored with software RAID.

explanation.summary: Hyperdisk Balanced High Availability is the Hyperdisk equivalent of a regional disk: writes are replicated synchronously to two zones, and the disk can be force-attached to a VM in the other zone.

option_breakdown.A: Snapshots give a daily RPO, not synchronous replication.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. Hyperdisk Balanced High Availability is the Hyperdisk equivalent of a regional disk: writes are replicated synchronously to two zones, and the disk can be force-attached to a VM in the other zone.
option_breakdown.C: Many newer machine series do not support Persistent Disk at all.
option_breakdown.D: Local SSD is lost when the VM stops; RAID within one VM does not add a zone.

questions.title: Sharing performance across many small Hyperdisks
questions.summary: Hyperdisk Storage Pools provision capacity and performance once and let many disks draw on it.
questions.question: A team runs 300 VMs, each with a Hyperdisk Balanced data disk sized for peak IOPS that it rarely reaches, so total provisioned performance is far above real use. What can reduce cost while letting each disk burst when needed?

options.A: Switch every disk to pd-standard.
options.B: Use Local SSD for every VM.
options.C: Create the disks in a Hyperdisk Storage Pool with pooled capacity and performance.
options.D: Take snapshots every hour and delete the disks.

explanation.summary: A storage pool is provisioned with total capacity and performance, and disks in it consume from the pool, so you pay for aggregate use rather than every disk's peak.

option_breakdown.A: Standard persistent disks lower cost but also performance, and newer series may not support them.
option_breakdown.B: Local SSD is ephemeral.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. A storage pool is provisioned with total capacity and performance, and disks in it consume from the pool, so you pay for aggregate use rather than every disk's peak.
option_breakdown.D: Deleting disks is not a storage strategy for running VMs.

questions.title: Getting scarce GPU VMs in whichever zone has them
questions.summary: Set the regional MIG's target distribution shape to ANY to place VMs where capacity exists.
questions.question: A regional managed instance group of GPU VMs for batch inference cannot reach its target size because one of its three zones has no capacity for that GPU. The workload does not need an even spread across zones. What should you change?

options.A: Convert it into three zonal groups, one per zone.
options.B: Raise the group's autoscaling maximum.
options.C: The group's target distribution shape to ANY.
options.D: Change the health check's unhealthy threshold.

explanation.summary: With the ANY shape, the group creates instances in whichever of its zones has capacity, instead of insisting on an even spread.

option_breakdown.A: More groups add management work and do not create capacity.
option_breakdown.B: A higher maximum does not help when a zone cannot supply the VMs.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. With the ANY shape, the group creates instances in whichever of its zones has capacity, instead of insisting on an even spread.
option_breakdown.D: Health checks are unrelated to placement.

explanation.gcloud_command:
gcloud compute instance-groups managed update infer-mig --region=us-central1 \
  --target-distribution-shape=ANY

questions.title: Keeping a required agent installed on every VM
questions.summary: An OS policy assignment declares desired state (packages, files) and VM Manager enforces it.
questions.question: Security requires a specific endpoint-protection package to be installed and running on every Linux VM labelled env=prod, including VMs created later and VMs where someone removes it. What should you use?

options.A: A one-time patch job that installs the package.
options.B: A VM Manager OS policy assignment targeting VMs with the label env=prod.
options.C: A startup script added to each existing instance template.
options.D: An organisation policy that requires the package.

explanation.summary: OS policy assignments define desired configuration and are continuously evaluated and enforced on matching VMs, including new ones.

option_breakdown.A: A patch job runs once; it does not restore a removed package.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. OS policy assignments define desired configuration and are continuously evaluated and enforced on matching VMs, including new ones.
option_breakdown.C: Startup scripts run only at boot and miss VMs not built from those templates.
option_breakdown.D: Organisation policies do not manage software inside guest operating systems.

explanation.gcloud_command:
gcloud compute os-config os-policy-assignments create edr-policy --location=us-central1-a \
  --file=edr-policy.yaml   # instanceFilter: inclusionLabels env=prod

questions.title: Spot VMs that should stop, not disappear
questions.summary: Set the instance termination action to STOP so a pre-empted Spot VM keeps its disks and can restart.
questions.question: A research team runs long simulations on Spot VMs with state on the boot disk. When a VM is pre-empted, they want to restart it later from where the disk left off, not rebuild it. How should the VMs be created?

options.A: With --provisioning-model=SPOT and --instance-termination-action=DELETE.
options.B: With --provisioning-model=SPOT and --instance-termination-action=STOP.
options.C: With --preemptible and automatic restart enabled.
options.D: As standard VMs with a Spot label.

explanation.summary: A Spot VM's termination action decides what pre-emption does: STOP keeps the VM and its disks so you can start it again later; DELETE removes the VM.

option_breakdown.A: DELETE removes the VM, and its boot disk too by default.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. A Spot VM's termination action decides what pre-emption does: STOP keeps the VM and its disks so you can start it again later; DELETE removes the VM.
option_breakdown.C: Pre-emptible and Spot VMs cannot use automatic restart.
option_breakdown.D: Labels do not change the provisioning model or price.

questions.title: Production clusters that upgrade conservatively
questions.summary: Enrol production clusters in the Stable release channel; use Regular or Rapid for earlier environments.
questions.question: A company wants production GKE clusters to receive Kubernetes versions only after they have been proven in the wider fleet, while its test clusters get new versions earlier. How should it enrol the clusters?

options.A: Production in the Stable release channel, test clusters in Regular or Rapid.
options.B: All clusters on a static version with auto-upgrade disabled.
options.C: Production in the Rapid channel so fixes arrive first.
options.D: No release channel, and upgrade production by hand each week.

explanation.summary: Release channels decide how soon a cluster receives new versions. Stable gets them last, after they have been proven in Rapid and Regular.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. Release channels decide how soon a cluster receives new versions. Stable gets them last, after they have been proven in Rapid and Regular.
option_breakdown.B: Static versions fall out of support and still get forced upgrades eventually.
option_breakdown.C: Rapid gets the newest, least-proven versions.
option_breakdown.D: Manual weekly upgrades are toil and easy to fall behind on.

questions.title: kubectl from anywhere without authorised networks or a bastion
questions.summary: The control plane's DNS-based endpoint is protected by IAM, so no IP allow-lists or proxies are needed.
questions.question: Engineers work from home and several clouds and need kubectl access to a GKE cluster whose control plane has no public IP-based access. The team wants to stop maintaining a bastion and IP allow-lists and rely on IAM. What should it enable?

options.A: Authorized networks listing every engineer's home IP.
options.B: The control plane's DNS-based endpoint, with access governed by IAM.
options.C: A public endpoint with no authorized networks.
options.D: An HA VPN tunnel from each engineer's laptop.

explanation.summary: The DNS-based endpoint gives every cluster a DNS name for its control plane. Requests are authorised with IAM, regardless of the caller's IP address, so no bastion or allow-list is needed.

option_breakdown.A: IP lists are exactly the maintenance being removed, and home IPs change.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. The DNS-based endpoint gives every cluster a DNS name for its control plane. Requests are authorised with IAM, regardless of the caller's IP address, so no bastion or allow-list is needed.
option_breakdown.C: A fully open public endpoint relies on credentials alone and widens exposure.
option_breakdown.D: HA VPN connects networks, not individual laptops.

explanation.gcloud_command:
gcloud container clusters update prod --location=europe-west1 --enable-dns-access
gcloud container clusters get-credentials prod --location=europe-west1 --dns-endpoint

questions.title: Keeping enough replicas up during node upgrades
questions.summary: A PodDisruptionBudget limits voluntary disruptions such as node drains during upgrades.
questions.question: During GKE node upgrades, nodes are drained, and sometimes all three replicas of a Deployment are evicted at about the same time, causing a short outage. What should you add?

options.A: A HorizontalPodAutoscaler with minReplicas: 3.
options.B: A liveness probe on the containers.
options.C: A node pool with auto-upgrade disabled.
options.D: A PodDisruptionBudget for the Deployment with minAvailable: 2.

explanation.summary: A PodDisruptionBudget tells Kubernetes how many Pods must stay available during voluntary disruptions, so drains wait instead of evicting too many at once.

option_breakdown.A: An HPA sets replica counts; it does not stop evictions.
option_breakdown.B: Liveness probes restart unhealthy containers; they do not limit evictions.
option_breakdown.C: Disabling upgrades avoids the drain but leaves the cluster unpatched.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. A PodDisruptionBudget tells Kubernetes how many Pods must stay available during voluntary disruptions, so drains wait instead of evicting too many at once.

questions.title: Reacting to a new Firestore document
questions.summary: Cloud Run functions can be triggered by Firestore document events through Eventarc.
questions.question: Whenever a document is created in the Firestore collection orders, a confirmation email must be sent. The team wants no polling and no servers. What should it deploy?

options.A: A Compute Engine VM that queries the collection every minute.
options.B: A Cloud Run function with an Eventarc trigger on the Firestore document-created event for orders/{id}.
options.C: A Cloud Scheduler job that calls a function every minute.
options.D: A Pub/Sub push subscription on the Firestore database.

explanation.summary: Firestore emits document events that Eventarc delivers to Cloud Run functions, so the function runs once per new order.

option_breakdown.A: Polling wastes resources and adds delay.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. Firestore emits document events that Eventarc delivers to Cloud Run functions, so the function runs once per new order.
option_breakdown.C: A schedule is still polling.
option_breakdown.D: Firestore does not publish to a Pub/Sub subscription by itself.

questions.title: Cloud Run reaching a private IP without a connector
questions.summary: Direct VPC egress sends a Cloud Run service's traffic into a VPC subnet with no connector VMs.
questions.question: A Cloud Run service must call an internal API on a VM's private IP in the prod VPC. The team wants the lowest latency and no extra instances to manage for the connection. What should it configure?

options.A: A Serverless VPC Access connector.
options.B: Direct VPC egress on the Cloud Run service, with a network and subnet.
options.C: A public IP on the VM with a firewall rule for Cloud Run's addresses.
options.D: Cloud NAT on the prod VPC.

explanation.summary: Direct VPC egress gives the service's instances IP addresses in your subnet, so traffic goes straight into the VPC without connector instances.

option_breakdown.A: A connector also works but runs connector instances you pay for and size.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. Direct VPC egress gives the service's instances IP addresses in your subnet, so traffic goes straight into the VPC without connector instances.
option_breakdown.C: Cloud Run has no fixed egress IPs to allow-list, and exposing the API publicly is unnecessary.
option_breakdown.D: NAT is for outbound internet traffic, not reaching private IPs.

questions.title: GPUs for a training job that can wait for capacity
questions.summary: Dynamic Workload Scheduler flex-start obtains GPUs for a job when capacity becomes available.
questions.question: A team needs eight H100 GPUs together for a six-hour fine-tuning job. It does not matter if the job starts a few hours later, but the GPUs must not be pre-empted mid-run and the team does not want a long reservation. What should it use?

options.A: Spot VMs with eight GPUs.
options.B: A one-year committed use discount for H100s.
options.C: Eight separate on-demand requests retried in a loop.
options.D: Dynamic Workload Scheduler in flex-start mode, which starts the job when all requested GPUs are available.

explanation.summary: Flex-start queues the request and provisions all the accelerators together when capacity is available, for a bounded run time, without pre-emption during the run.

option_breakdown.A: Spot VMs can be pre-empted at any time.
option_breakdown.B: A commitment is a long-term purchase for steady use.
option_breakdown.C: Retrying one by one can leave the job holding some GPUs idle while waiting for the rest.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. Flex-start queues the request and provisions all the accelerators together when capacity is available, for a bounded run time, without pre-emption during the run.

explanation.gcloud_command: # GKE: a node pool with --flex-start (or a ProvisioningRequest); Compute Engine: a flex-start MIG resize request

questions.title: Intrusion prevention between tiers
questions.summary: Cloud NGFW Enterprise inspects traffic through a firewall endpoint with a security profile group.
questions.question: Compliance now requires intrusion detection and prevention for traffic from the application tier to the database tier inside a VPC, not just allow/deny by port. What should you configure?

options.A: Cloud NGFW Enterprise: a firewall endpoint for the zone, a security profile group with threat prevention, and a policy rule with the action apply_security_profile_group.
options.B: A VPC firewall rule with logging enabled.
options.C: Cloud Armor on the database's internal load balancer.
options.D: VPC Flow Logs with 100% sampling.

explanation.summary: Cloud NGFW Enterprise adds Layer 7 intrusion prevention. Matching traffic is sent to a firewall endpoint and inspected against the security profile.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. Cloud NGFW Enterprise adds Layer 7 intrusion prevention. Matching traffic is sent to a firewall endpoint and inspected against the security profile.
option_breakdown.B: Logging records connections; it detects and blocks no intrusions.
option_breakdown.C: Cloud Armor protects load-balanced traffic from the internet, not east-west traffic to databases.
option_breakdown.D: Flow logs are telemetry, not prevention.

questions.title: Forty partner ranges used in six rules
questions.summary: An address group holds a reusable list of IP ranges that firewall policy rules reference.
questions.question: Six firewall policy rules must each allow the same 40 partner IP ranges, and the list changes monthly. Editing all six rules every month causes mistakes. What should you use?

options.A: A network tag named partners.
options.B: An address group with the 40 ranges, referenced by all six rules.
options.C: A secure tag applied to the partner ranges.
options.D: One rule with priority 0 that allows all 40 ranges to everything.

explanation.summary: Address groups are reusable collections of IP ranges for firewall policies. Updating the group updates every rule that references it.

option_breakdown.A: Network tags identify your VMs; they cannot represent external IP ranges.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. Address groups are reusable collections of IP ranges for firewall policies. Updating the group updates every rule that references it.
option_breakdown.C: Secure tags are attached to your resources, not to external address ranges.
option_breakdown.D: One broad rule loses the per-destination scope of the six rules.

questions.title: A secure tag that will not work in a second VPC
questions.subtopic: Secure Tags and Service Accounts in Rules
questions.summary: A firewall-purpose tag key is scoped to one VPC network through its purpose data.
questions.question: A secure tag key tier was created with the GCE_FIREWALL purpose for the network vpc-prod. Engineers try to use tier=web in a firewall policy rule for vpc-staging, and the rule never matches. Why?

options.A: Secure tags can only be used in hierarchical firewall policies.
options.B: The tag value must first be attached to the vpc-staging network itself.
options.C: The tag key's purpose data binds it to vpc-prod; vpc-staging needs its own firewall tag key.
options.D: Secure tags only match after the VMs are restarted twice.

explanation.summary: A tag key created for firewall use is scoped to a VPC network (or organisation, depending on its purpose data). It can only be used by firewall policies for that network.

option_breakdown.A: Secure tags work in global and regional network firewall policies as well.
option_breakdown.B: Tag values are attached to VM instances, not to networks.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. A tag key created for firewall use is scoped to a VPC network (or organisation, depending on its purpose data). It can only be used by firewall policies for that network.
option_breakdown.D: There is no such restart requirement.

explanation.gcloud_command:
gcloud resource-manager tags keys create tier-stg --parent=organizations/ORG_ID \
  --purpose=GCE_FIREWALL --purpose-data=network=P/vpc-staging

questions.title: Transitive connectivity among many VPCs
questions.summary: Network Connectivity Center with VPC spokes connects many VPCs through a hub, unlike non-transitive peering.
questions.question: Twelve VPC networks in different projects must all reach each other privately. A full mesh of VPC peerings would need 66 connections and still hits peering limits. What should the network team use?

options.A: A Network Connectivity Center hub with each VPC attached as a VPC spoke.
options.B: VPC Network Peering from every VPC to one central VPC.
options.C: Cloud NAT in every VPC.
options.D: External IP addresses on every VM with firewall rules.

explanation.summary: An NCC hub with VPC spokes exchanges subnet routes among all attached VPCs, giving any-to-any connectivity without a peering mesh.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. An NCC hub with VPC spokes exchanges subnet routes among all attached VPCs, giving any-to-any connectivity without a peering mesh.
option_breakdown.B: Peering is not transitive, so spokes still could not reach each other through the centre.
option_breakdown.C: NAT gives outbound internet access; it does not connect VPCs.
option_breakdown.D: Public exposure is not private connectivity.

explanation.gcloud_command:
gcloud network-connectivity hubs create corp-hub
gcloud network-connectivity spokes linked-vpc-network create vpc-a --hub=corp-hub --global \
  --vpc-network=projects/P-A/global/networks/vpc-a

questions.title: An internal service that must fail over between regions
questions.summary: A cross-region internal Application Load Balancer serves internal clients from backends in several regions.
questions.question: An internal HTTP service runs in us-east1 and us-west1. Internal clients should use one internal address, and if the us-east1 backends fail, traffic should go to us-west1 automatically. What load balancer fits?

options.A: A regional internal Application Load Balancer in us-east1.
options.B: A global external Application Load Balancer.
options.C: An internal passthrough Network Load Balancer.
options.D: A cross-region internal Application Load Balancer.

explanation.summary: The cross-region internal Application Load Balancer has backends in several regions and fails over between them for internal clients.

option_breakdown.A: A regional load balancer's backends are all in one region.
option_breakdown.B: An external load balancer exposes the service to the internet.
option_breakdown.C: The passthrough Network Load Balancer is regional and Layer 4.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. The cross-region internal Application Load Balancer has backends in several regions and fails over between them for internal clients.

explanation.gcloud_command:
gcloud compute backend-services create svc-bs --global --load-balancing-scheme=INTERNAL_MANAGED --protocol=HTTP
gcloud compute forwarding-rules create svc-fr-east --global --load-balancing-scheme=INTERNAL_MANAGED \
  --network=prod --subnet=proxy-east --subnet-region=us-east1 --target-http-proxy=svc-proxy --ports=80

questions.title: How many tunnels an HA VPN to AWS needs
questions.summary: For the 99.99% SLA to AWS, the HA VPN gateway's two interfaces connect to two AWS VPN connections: four tunnels.
questions.question: You are connecting an HA VPN gateway to an AWS virtual private gateway and must meet Google Cloud's 99.99% HA VPN SLA. Each AWS site-to-site VPN connection provides two tunnel endpoints. How should you build it?

options.A: One AWS VPN connection and two tunnels, one from each HA VPN interface.
options.B: One AWS VPN connection and one tunnel with static routes.
options.C: Two AWS VPN connections, each terminated on a separate Classic VPN gateway.
options.D: Create two AWS site-to-site VPN connections and four tunnels, two from each HA VPN interface, with BGP sessions on a Cloud Router.

explanation.summary: The documented HA topology for AWS uses two AWS VPN connections (four outside IP addresses) so that each HA VPN interface has two tunnels; that redundancy is what the 99.99% configuration requires.

option_breakdown.A: Two tunnels to one AWS connection leave a single AWS-side connection as a point of failure and do not match the SLA topology.
option_breakdown.B: A single static tunnel is neither redundant nor dynamically routed.
option_breakdown.C: Classic VPN is not covered by the 99.99% SLA.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. The documented HA topology for AWS uses two AWS VPN connections (four outside IP addresses) so that each HA VPN interface has two tunnels; that redundancy is what the 99.99% configuration requires.

explanation.gcloud_command:
gcloud compute external-vpn-gateways create aws-gw --interfaces=0=AWS_IP_1,1=AWS_IP_2,2=AWS_IP_3,3=AWS_IP_4
gcloud compute vpn-tunnels create t0 --vpn-gateway=gcp-to-aws --interface=0 --peer-external-gateway=aws-gw \
  --peer-external-gateway-interface=0 --region=us-east4 --ike-version=2 --shared-secret=S --router=aws-router

questions.title: Terraform state for a team, not a laptop
questions.summary: Store Terraform state in a Cloud Storage backend, which also provides state locking.
questions.question: Three engineers run Terraform against the same environment, and state files on their laptops have diverged, leading to conflicting changes. What should they configure?

options.A: A gcs backend that stores state in a versioned Cloud Storage bucket, with its built-in state locking.
options.B: Commit terraform.tfstate to the Git repository after every apply.
options.C: Run terraform refresh before every plan.
options.D: Give each engineer a separate workspace in the same local directory.

explanation.summary: A remote gcs backend gives one shared state with locking, so two applies cannot run at once; bucket versioning allows recovery of earlier state.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. A remote gcs backend gives one shared state with locking, so two applies cannot run at once; bucket versioning allows recovery of earlier state.
option_breakdown.B: State in Git is often stale, can conflict, and may contain secrets.
option_breakdown.C: Refresh updates state from real resources but does not share or lock it.
option_breakdown.D: Workspaces on one laptop do not share state across engineers.

questions.title: Turning a console form into gcloud or Terraform
questions.summary: The console's Equivalent code view shows the gcloud, Terraform or REST version of what you configured.
questions.question: An engineer configured a complex VM in the console's create form and now wants the same configuration as code for the team's pipeline, without clicking Create. What is the quickest way?

options.A: Create the VM, then write the Terraform by reading the instance's details page.
options.B: Export Admin Activity audit logs after creating the VM.
options.C: Open Equivalent code in the create form and copy the gcloud command or Terraform it shows.

explanation.summary: Many console create forms show equivalent code for the current settings, which gives an exact starting point for automation without creating the resource.

option_breakdown.B: Audit logs record the API request, not ready-to-use Terraform, and need the VM created.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. Many console create forms show equivalent code for the current settings, which gives an exact starting point for automation without creating the resource.
